comments.text:
It’s honestly hard to figure out what platforms should be doing to protect people. Part of me misses the old days of Tumblr, Instagram, and Facebook, when things felt more open. There were fewer ads, more community, and a real sense of freedom. You could find anything, go anywhere online, and just exist in it. I was a kid on Tumblr reposting the wildest stuff, and it felt like the internet was something you explored, not something that was curated for you.

But we don’t live in that version of the internet anymore.

Now, what we see isn’t the full conversation; it’s a version of it. There’s an inherent bias in the content we’re shown because we’re not just browsing freely anymore… we’re being guided. Guided by algorithms, by platforms trying to protect users, and by systems designed to decide what we should and shouldn’t see. And the more these platforms try to protect us, the more control they have over what reaches us. 

I think that’s a big problem today. We’re not really seeing the other side or hearing their full perspective. By the time we even get close to having a real conversation, by the time we arrive at that metaphorical table, we’re already defensive, already frustrated, already ready to hurt each other over conversations that we never actually had.It just feels like we’re living in a time where people aren’t talking with each other anymore… just reacting to pieces of each other. And yeah… that’s freaking troubling.
